entries.note: “I think” qualifies the imminent-release prediction as a tentative belief.

entries.test: Public evaluations of GPT-5 guardrails showing whether jailbreaks bypass them and benign requests receive unwarranted refusals would test the prediction.
entries.note: The possibility language concerns guardrail presence; the prediction about their failures is firm.

entries.test: Public reproducible tests of GPT-5 natural-language output connected simply and directly to databases or virtual assistants would establish whether downstream behavior is reliable and predictable.
entries.note: The restriction to simple, direct connections matters; systems with substantial external validation would not directly test it.

entries.test: GPT-5's public interface documentation and reproducible integration tests would show whether programmers can access reliable representations of its subjects that reliably feed downstream processes.
entries.note: The claim concerns externally accessible models and their practical reliability.

entries.test: Public controlled evaluations of GPT-5 without external aids against Cicero in Diplomacy, in autonomous driving, and in varied household robot tasks would test the three capability predictions.
entries.note: Rosie supplies a loose reference for versatile household assistance. The explicit restriction on external aids must be preserved.
“May be seen” states a possible retrospective assessment rather than a firm outcome.

entries.test: Public architectural documentation of a demonstrated trustworthy, human-aligned general AI would show whether it incorporates greater structure, built-in knowledge, and explicit reasoning and planning tools than GPT-style systems.
entries.note: The architectural prediction is firm, conditional on such AI arriving, and has no deadline.

entries.test: Intellectual historians' published retrospectives in 2043 would show whether they conclude that early AI research overemphasized LLMs before a critical shift toward more structured systems with deeper comprehension.
entries.note: The test concerns historians' published conclusions, even though those conclusions contain evaluative terms.
“Shiniest” is a promotional metaphor without a testable ranking. The remainder rejects an inference rather than firmly predicting GPT-5's place on an optimal path.
